While Frozen Section (FS) was commonly used in patients undergoing thyroidectomy at our institution, in no patient over the last decade did FS correctly alter the intraoperative management. Given the time required to perform FS and the cost associated with it, we believe that routine FS should not be performed in these patients.

In other words, Frozen Section is not typically used as part of the standard surgical management for multinodular thyroid disease due to its limitations, including the potential delay in diagnosis, high cost, and limited effectiveness. Instead, surgeons may use alternative diagnostic methods, such as fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB), to diagnose and stage the disease before performing surgery.
